result.summary: The street features a mix of pedestrian infrastructure, including a recently upgraded wide sidewalk with protective bollards on the right side and a narrower, older walkway on the left. The roadway lacks lane markings and marked crosswalks at the upcoming intersection, which is controlled by stop signs. The environment is primarily residential with buildings situated directly at the sidewalk edge.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks painted crosswalks, reducing driver awareness of pedestrian crossing points.

hazards.name: Lack of Lane Markings
hazards.description: The absence of lane lines on a relatively wide street can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable positioning.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right curbs near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install ladder or zebra-style crosswalk markings at the intersection to clearly designate pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility for all users.

interventions.title: Lane Striping
interventions.description: Apply paint to define travel lanes and parking zones, which helps organize traffic and can naturally reduce vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk in a residential or mixed-use area. Yellow bollards are installed along the curb to prevent vehicle encroachment, providing a degree of physical protection despite the lack of a landscaped buffer.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the roadway without a planting strip or furniture zone, though bollards mitigate some risk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground

hazards.name: Blank frontage
hazards.description: The solid green wall and side of the building reduce passive surveillance and visual interest for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the sidewalk edge

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a planting strip to create a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the street, improving comfort and safety.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to ensure the wide walkway is well-illuminated for nighttime safety.

result.summary: A narrow residential street lined with row houses and continuous sidewalks on both sides. The environment lacks formal pedestrian crossings and traffic calming measures, with large parked vehicles creating significant sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: A large white box van parked on the left side of the street significantly blocks visibility between pedestrians on the sidewalk and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs along this stretch of the street, increasing risk for mid-block crossings.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions near intersections and potential crossing points to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install speed humps or cushions to physically reduce vehicle speeds in this residential area.

result.summary: A residential mid-block environment with narrow, poorly maintained sidewalks directly adjacent to the roadway. There is no physical buffer between pedestrians and vehicles, and utility poles further obstruct the walking path.

hazards.name: Poor Sidewalk Condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk is heavily cracked with significant weed growth, creating uneven surfaces and tripping hazards.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is positioned on the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the effective walking width for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the narrow sidewalk and the active travel lane.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and level the sidewalk surface to provide a continuous, ADA-compliant walking path free of tripping hazards.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Green Infrastructure
interventions.description: Install street trees or planters to provide a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, improving safety and comfort.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles to the furniture zone or underground to maximize the clear walking width of the sidewalk.
